name: IL-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: District fundamentals: a D+19 Chicago-area seat that rarely sees competitive general elections
Quigley's financial edge: roughly $1.1 million on hand against a challenger with no reported fundraising
Incumbency: Quigley was renominated and carries the usual incumbent advantage
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 95%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Quigley: a D+19 district, a long-serving incumbent with over $1.1 million banked, and a Republican challenger showing no measurable fundraising or outside support. Markets at 95% Democratic corroborate a race with no visible path for an upset.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal involving Quigley or a sudden national shift toward Republicans could narrow the margin, though the district's partisan lean makes an actual upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Illinois' 5th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, and Mike Quigley has held it comfortably since 2009. He enters the general election with about $1.1 million in cash on hand, while Republican Tommy Hanson shows no reported fundraising or outside spending to mount a challenge.

There is no public polling of the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the financial imbalance, and prediction markets, which price Quigley's chances near 95%. Every available signal points in the same direction: a deep-blue urban seat, an entrenched incumbent, and an underfunded challenger. The main uncertainty is the absence of direct polling, which leaves some room for error in the exact margin, but not enough to change the expected outcome. Quigley is strongly favored to win another term.
